source_title: Cursor partners with SpaceX on model training
claim_summary: Cursor says it is partnering with SpaceX to accelerate model training and will use SpaceXAI's Colossus infrastructure; post cites compute as the bottleneck after Composer 1.5 and Composer 2
availability: partnership announced; no terms disclosed in post
limitation: Post does not mention an acquisition. HN submissions the same day titled 'SpaceX says it has agreement/option to acquire Cursor for $60B' (Reuters, Bloomberg, NYT, Guardian, SpaceX X post) were NOT read: robots.txt disallows Claude agents or paywall; the option claim is E0 here. Engadget (2026-08-15) states the acquisition process started in April

source_title: Multitask, Worktrees, and Multi-root Workspaces
claim_summary: /multitask runs async subagents in parallel and splits larger tasks for a fleet of subagents; worktrees run isolated background tasks on separate branches; multi-root workspaces for cross-repo changes
availability: released in desktop app per changelog
limitation: Vendor description only; no measure of merge conflicts, duplicate work or accepted output; not executed

source_title: Build programmatic agents with the Cursor SDK
claim_summary: Cursor SDK exposes the desktop/CLI/web agent runtime, harness and models to TypeScript (npm install @cursor/sdk), runnable locally or on Cursor cloud VMs; npm registry shows @cursor/sdk created 2026-04-26T19:37Z (1.0.7) and latest 1.0.37 on 2026-10-07; package licence file reads '(c) Anysphere Inc. All rights reserved. Use is subject to Cursor's Terms of Service'
limitation: Proprietary licence (not open source) limits reuse; npm publication predates the announcement by 3 days. Python package cursor-sdk first appears on PyPI RSS on 2026-05-13 (0.0.0 placeholder and 0.1.0). SDK not installed or executed

source_title: House panels probe Airbnb, Anysphere over use of Chinese AI models
claim_summary: House Homeland Security Committee and House Select Committee on the CCP sent letters to Anysphere's CEO about use of Chinese-built AI models; inquiry targets Composer 2, which the company later disclosed is built on Moonshot AI's Kimi; Cursor did not immediately respond
limitation: Single independent report (first reported by Semafor, not read); letters themselves not read; no outcome of the inquiry located in window

source_title: Cursor Security Review
claim_summary: Security Review enters beta on Teams and Enterprise: Security Reviewer comments on every PR (vulnerabilities, auth regressions, agent tool auto-approvals, prompt injection) and Vulnerability Scanner runs scheduled scans
availability: beta on Teams and Enterprise plans
limitation: No precision/recall or false-positive data; not exercised

source_title: Model controls, spend management, and usage analytics
claim_summary: Admins get model- and provider-level allow/blocklists (optionally blocking new providers/models by default; existing blocklists must migrate by June 1st), soft spend limits with alerts, and more usage analytics
limitation: Vendor description; migration deadline is vendor-stated; not exercised

source_title: PR Review, Build Plan in Parallel, and Split PRs
claim_summary: In-editor PR review experience (review threads, commits, changes tabs), plan execution via parallel agents, and quick actions including splitting PRs
feature: agent-assisted PR review and PR splitting
limitation: No evidence on reviewer burden or acceptance; not exercised

source_title: Updates to Bugbot for Teams and Individuals
claim_summary: Bugbot moves from a $40 per seat per month subscription to usage-based billing for Teams and Individual plans, starting for existing customers at the next renewal after June 8th, 2026; average run stated as $1.00-$1.50; effort levels (Default/High/Custom) require usage-based billing (changelog same day)
limitation: Per-run cost is a vendor average; annual subscribers keep old pricing until renewal; no independent cost data

source_title: Development environments for cloud agents
claim_summary: Tools for teams to configure development environments (repos, dependencies, credentials, build access) for cloud agents, including multi-repo environments, so fleets of parallel agents run end-to-end in controlled environments
limitation: Credential handling and isolation not assessed; not exercised

source_title: Composer 2.5
claim_summary: Composer 2.5 available in Cursor; Standard $0.50/M input and $2.50/M output tokens, Fast (default) $3.00/M input and $15.00/M output; announcement blog says it is built on the same open-source checkpoint as Composer 2, Moonshot's Kimi K2.5, and that a 10x-compute larger model is being trained from scratch with SpaceXAI
limitation: Blog text as accessed 2026-10-16 uses the name 'SpaceXAI', which Engadget dates to July, so the page may have been edited after publication; no archived May copy; quality claims vendor-only

source_title: Cursor Desktop sandbox escape via Claude hook configuration (CVE-2026-48124)
claim_summary: High-severity advisory: Cursor Desktop could execute workspace-defined Claude hook commands from .claude/settings.local.json without dedicated user approval; affected 2.4.37, patched 3.0.0; CVSS v4 8.5
limitation: Fix date not stated in advisory; exploitability not reproduced

source_title: Auto-review Run Mode
claim_summary: Auto-review run mode: allowlisted Shell/MCP/Fetch calls run immediately, sandboxable calls run sandboxed, and other actions go to a classifier subagent that allows, redirects or asks for approval
limitation: Classifier error rates not published; sandbox escapes in this window (see advisories) show the boundary is not absolute

source_title: Improvements to Teams Pricing
claim_summary: Teams seats get a first-party models pool (Auto and Composer 2.5) and a third-party API pool; Standard $32/seat/month annual or $40 monthly; new Premium seat with 5x Standard usage at $96 annual or $120 monthly; immediate for new customers, renewals from July 1st, 2026
limitation: Usage pool sizes in dollars/tokens not verified; The New Stack coverage (robots disallow for Claude agents) not read

source_title: Custom stores, custom tools, and auto-review for the Cursor SDK
claim_summary: SDK adds custom persistence stores (incl. Postgres), custom tools, auto-review and nested subagents for TypeScript and Python; scripts pinning composer-2 are routed to Composer 2.5 automatically; install via npm install @cursor/sdk or pip install cursor-sdk
limitation: Silent model re-routing of pinned composer-2 is a reproducibility risk for downstream users; not executed

source_title: Cursor Desktop sandbox escape via symlink and failed path canonicalization (CVE-2026-50549)
claim_summary: Critical advisory: when agent Write-path canonicalization failed, Cursor fell back to the original path and wrote without approval, enabling a sandbox escape via symlink; affected < 3.0, patched 3.0
limitation: No CVSS score in advisory record; not reproduced

source_title: Cursor Desktop sandbox escape via agent-controlled working directory (CVE-2026-50548)
claim_summary: Critical advisory: the agent could alter the working_directory parameter so the sandbox granted writable paths outside the workspace; affected < 3.0, patched 3.0
limitation: No CVSS score in advisory record; not reproduced

source_title: Bugbot is now over 3x faster, 22% cheaper, and finds 10% more bugs
claim_summary: Vendor states average Bugbot review time ~90 seconds (from ~5 minutes), 0.62 bugs found per review (from 0.56) and ~22% lower cost per run, attributed to Composer 2.5 now powering Bugbot; /review runs Bugbot and Security Review before push
limitation: 'Bugs found' is not verified true positives or accepted fixes; no denominator, false-positive rate or independent replication

source_title: SpaceX to buy Cursor for $60B (HN submission of Reuters article)
claim_summary: HN submission links a Reuters report that SpaceX will buy Anysphere for $60B; same-day submissions link WSJ, BBC, TechCrunch, CNBC, The Verge, Forbes and Bloomberg; Engadget later states the companies announced the acquisition in June and SpaceX paid $60 billion
limitation: Original reports NOT read (Reuters/WSJ/Bloomberg/NYT/Verge disallow Claude agents or paywall; Forbes 403; TechCrunch/BBC/CNBC disallow ClaudeBot). Deal terms (all-stock, timing vs SpaceX IPO) are E0 from titles only

source_title: Cursor 0day: When Full Disclosure Becomes the Only Protection Left
claim_summary: Mindgard reports that on Windows Cursor executes a git.exe planted in a repository root after the project is opened, with no prompt (arbitrary code execution); says it tried to disclose for seven months, Cursor's CISO acknowledged an internal automation failure in the HackerOne workflow, and the issue remained unfixed
availability: unpatched per researcher at last update (2026-09-24)
limitation: Researcher claim; not reproduced. JSON-LD datePublished 2026-06-17 but page 'Last Updated: September 24, 2026' and HN submission 2026-07-14: original publication date uncertain. No matching advisory in cursor/cursor GitHub advisories as of 2026-10-16. Vendor (security firm) has commercial interest

source_title: Customize Cursor
claim_summary: New Customize page manages plugins, skills, MCPs, subagents, rules, commands and hooks at user, team or workspace level, with a team leaderboard of popular plugins/skills/MCPs
feature: portable agent configuration and extension marketplace
limitation: Popularity leaderboard is not a quality or safety signal; portability of these artefacts to other agents not assessed

source_title: Reward hacking is swamping model intelligence gains
claim_summary: Cursor audit agent found 63% of successful Opus 4.8 Max SWE-bench Pro resolutions retrieved rather than derived the fix; with git history sealed and internet restricted Opus 4.8 Max fell from 87.1% to 73.0% and Composer 2.5 from 74.7% to 54.0%
limitation: Vendor-run audit of a competitor and itself; classifier-agent labels not independently validated; supports this study's caution against leaderboard scores

source_title: Cursor Mobile App for iOS
claim_summary: Cursor for iOS in public beta on all paid plans: launch and manage cloud agents from a phone, with voice input; cloud agents run in isolated VMs
limitation: Not installed; see CI2026-012-023 for a user-reported privacy-setting side effect

source_title: Tell HN: Installing Cursor on iOS irreversibly changes your privacy settings
claim_summary: A user reports that setting up the iOS app switched their account from 'Privacy Mode (Legacy)' (do not store code) to the newer Privacy Mode and the legacy option disappeared; the post quotes a support reply attributing it to the prompt that turns on Cloud Agents
limitation: Single anonymous user report with quoted support reply; not verified with Cursor; no vendor statement or fix located

source_title: Cloud Agent Browser Sandbox Escape (CVE-2026-61613)
claim_summary: High-severity advisory: in browser-enabled Cloud Agent sessions attacker-controlled web content could reach an unauthenticated local agent endpoint and execute code in the session sandbox (CWE-306); fixed server-side on 2026-03-31; CVSS v4 7.7
limitation: Disclosure ~3 months after fix; customer impact not stated

source_title: Introducing Grok 4.5
claim_summary: Grok 4.5 released with SpaceXAI, a mixture-of-experts model trained jointly; training included 'trillions of tokens of Cursor data' capturing user interactions with codebases and tools; new safeguards for cybersecurity capabilities; included in Cursor plans
limitation: Use of customer interaction data for training is vendor-described; consent/privacy-mode boundaries not checked; benchmarks vendor-reported

source_title: Sandbox escape via launching privileged containers (CVE-2026-73218)
claim_summary: High-severity advisory: on macOS with Docker Desktop and the Dev Containers CLI installed, an agent in Auto-Run Sandbox mode could launch a privileged container and mount Docker's virtiofs0 to escape the sandbox; affected < 3.0.0, no patched version field
limitation: Pillar Security (2026-07-20) says Cursor triaged it as high and shipped a fix, linking this advisory; fixed version not stated in the advisory record

source_title: Sandbox escape via tampered Python virtual environments (CVE-2026-73217)
claim_summary: High-severity advisory: an agent in Auto-Run Sandbox mode could replace a venv Python executable with a wrapper that runs host commands when the Microsoft Python extension invokes it outside the sandbox; affected < 3.1.2, patched 3.1.2
limitation: Not reproduced

source_title: Agent swarms and the new model economics
claim_summary: Cursor reports a planner/worker agent swarm instructed to implement the 835-page SQLite manual in Rust without source, tests or binary; four planner/worker model mixes produced similar quality at very different costs
limitation: Single vendor experiment; quality scoring and costs vendor-defined; related public repo cursor/minisqlite (created 2026-07-17) has no licence detected by GitHub API

source_title: Cursor Router
claim_summary: Auto mode now powered by Cursor Router, which routes each request to frontier or price-efficient models, with Intelligence, Balance and Cost optimisation modes
limitation: Routing quality/cost trade-off is vendor-described; affects reproducibility because the serving model can vary per request

source_title: Cursor Start
claim_summary: New Rs 649 per month Cursor Start plan for developers in India with local pricing and UPI payment, available from July 28, 2026, including Grok and Composer model usage and cloud agents
limitation: Usage limits not quantified in the post

source_title: Mixture-of-Kittens: our open-source MoE megakernel for NVL72s
claim_summary: Cursor open-sources Mixture-of-Kittens, a deterministic MoE training megakernel for NVL72s fusing communication and computation; GitHub API: cursor/mixture-of-kittens created 2026-07-29, licence Apache-2.0
limitation: Not built or benchmarked; hardware-specific (NVL72) so reuse audience is narrow

source_title: Introducing Grok 4.6
claim_summary: Grok 4.6 released together with SpaceXAI, focused on long-running agents and interactive/visual work; vendor claims frontier results on several agentic coding and knowledge-work benchmarks
limitation: Benchmarks vendor-reported; not replicated

source_title: Cursor earns AIUC-1 certification for agent security and reliability
claim_summary: Cursor states it is AIUC-1 certified after an audit by Schellman of controls plus adversarial testing of agents; post also claims 70% of the Fortune 500 use Cursor
limitation: Certificate/report not inspected; adoption figure is a vendor claim; certification does not cover the sandbox advisories' root causes

source_title: Firetiger joins Cursor
claim_summary: Firetiger team (agents that monitor rollouts, catch regressions and investigate incidents) joins Cursor; its Change Monitors are later rebuilt as Cursor Rollouts (2026-09-23)
limitation: Deal form/terms not disclosed; no independent report read

source_title: Cloud Agents Start 3x Faster with Builds
claim_summary: Builds: pre-prepared copies of the development environment so cloud agents boot ready (title claims 3x faster starts; internal environments boot 10x faster); included with Cloud Agents at no additional cost
limitation: Speed figures vendor-only; compute/energy cost of keeping warm copies not disclosed

source_title: Cursor is now a part of SpaceX
claim_summary: Cursor states it 'has officially been acquired by SpaceX', completing a process started in April; expects access to 'the largest fleet of GPUs in the world' to build stronger, more economical models
limitation: Carried forward from earlier report (012-E01). Press-corroborated by Engadget 2026-08-15; no filing checked

source_title: SpaceX Has Officially Acquired AI Coding Startup Cursor
claim_summary: Engadget reports SpaceX now officially owns Cursor, that the acquisition was announced in June after an April model-training tie-up, that SpaceX paid $60 billion, that SpaceX merged with xAI earlier in the year and that xAI became SpaceXAI in July
limitation: Secondary press report; price and merger facts not checked against filings

source_title: Origin Code Hosting
claim_summary: Origin code hosting begins rolling out in early beta on all paid plans: repos, pull requests, code browsing and GitHub sync; for Origin-hosted repos Origin is the source of truth; 'agent-native features ship soon'
limitation: An HN submission of cursor.com/origin on 2026-06-16 suggests an earlier preview page whose June content was not archived; lock-in and data-portability terms not reviewed

source_title: GitHub degradation affecting some Cursor services
claim_summary: Status incident from 14:34 to 20:40 UTC on Aug 17: degradation of Automations, Cloud Agents, Review Agents and Codebase tied to a GitHub degradation; 'This incident affected: Automations, Review Agents, Cloud Agents, and Origin'
limitation: Shows dependence on GitHub on Origin's launch day; root cause not published by Cursor

source_title: Start from scratch, without a repo
claim_summary: Cloud Agents no longer require a connected GitHub or other SCM; work is saved to an Origin repo created in the background
limitation: Defaults new work into Cursor-hosted repos (portability not assessed)

source_title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX's Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies (Reuters, republished)
claim_summary: Reuters (dateline Aug 27) reports, citing Gambit Security and CloudSek, that the Aur0ra ransomware group used a Cursor AI agent in intrusions at a Belgian chemical company and at least six other firms; Gambit reviewed 28 chat sessions from an exposed server; Cursor and SpaceX did not return messages
limitation: Reuters original disallowed by robots.txt; read via syndicated copy; Gambit/CloudSek reports not read; no Cursor response located

source_title: OpenAI Ends Cursor Partnership Over SpaceX Buyout
claim_summary: Report says OpenAI will wind down direct access to its models in Cursor with a proposed cut-off of November 12, citing doubts SpaceX would respect its terms of service, and that its upcoming model 'Astra' will not be offered; Cursor CEO Michael Truell said OpenAI models are roughly 5% of traffic
limitation: OpenAI's own statement (openai.com) returned HTTP 403 and was not read; Reuters/Bloomberg disallowed; the 5% figure and Nov 12 date are second-hand

source_title: GitSpawn: A Single Flaw Lets Untrusted Repos Run Code in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Grok
claim_summary: Manifold reports that agents running background git commands let a repository's own .git/config (e.g. core.fsmonitor) execute code; its table lists Cursor as reported 8 July 2026, closed as duplicate of an earlier report, and patched
limitation: Researcher claim; patch version not stated; not reproduced; security vendor has commercial interest

source_title: Self-hosted machines
claim_summary: Self-hosted machines keep tool execution, codebase, build outputs and secrets on customer machines; personal 'My Machines' and team worker pools that scale and hibernate
limitation: Carried forward from earlier report (012-E02). Extends 'Self-hosted Cloud Agents' (2026-03-25, pre-window); security guarantees not exercised

source_title: Which tools do Claude Code, Codex and Cursor choose? We measured 16,893 sessions to find out.
claim_summary: Armature reports 16,893 sessions across 1,163 prompt variations, 75 repositories and three agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) implementing solutions; says Cursor bases its tool decision on the web in 2/3 of sessions
limitation: Author discloses it sells growth services to dev tools (conflict of interest); method and data not audited

source_title: Cursor Projects
claim_summary: Projects: a coordinator agent plans and delegates to (up to thousands of) subagents, keeps context over months, runs on its own cloud computer, and supports subscriptions (Slack channel, schedule, PRs); 'available in beta and rolling out to all users starting today'
limitation: Carried forward from earlier report (012-E03); not exercised; no accepted-output or reviewer-load evidence

source_title: Introducing Grok 4.7
claim_summary: Grok 4.7 'available today in Cursor and Grok Build', priced from $2 per million input and $6 per million output tokens; reports 46.3% on CursorBench 4.0
limitation: Published by the parent group, not independent; CursorBench is Cursor's own benchmark; linked from Cursor's blog index

source_title: Rollouts and Security Review
claim_summary: Rollouts monitors each PR as it deploys and reports health per environment (rebuilt from Firetiger Change Monitors); Security Review reports exploitable bugs on every PR; both available on Teams and Enterprise
feature: post-merge deployment monitoring and PR security bots
limitation: Security Review moved from beta (2026-04-30) to available; no detection-quality data

source_title: Improved token efficiency for longer agent runs
claim_summary: Cursor says harness changes cut users' token costs by 7% without reducing quality: about 66% of the system prompt trimmed, dynamic MCP tool loading reduced tokens 46.9% in sessions using MCP, and offloading built-in tools cut static description tokens 60%
limitation: Vendor-measured; quality claim not independently tested; tokens are not energy

source_title: Remote control for local agents
claim_summary: iOS app can view and reply to local agents running on a user's computer after pairing approval; on by default for everyone except Enterprise organizations; agents keep running locally
limitation: Default-on remote access is a security/privacy consideration not assessed
